# Transit MCP

> Transit MCP is a free, anonymous, read-only Model Context Protocol (MCP) server for DC Metro and NYC Subway trip planning and real-time transit information. SF Bay support is in development and is not available through public tools. Transit MCP was formerly Metro MCP; it is the same server.

- MCP endpoint (Streamable HTTP): https://transitmcp.com/mcp
- Legacy endpoint, still supported: https://metro-mcp.anuragd.me/mcp
- Authentication: none. No login, API key, bearer token, or OAuth flow is required. Stale Authorization headers are ignored.
- Server description (JSON): https://transitmcp.com/info
- Works with Claude, Cursor, Codex, Gemini, and any MCP client that speaks Streamable HTTP.
- ChatGPT plugin listing: https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a9078f4d6dc8191be735cc1c2ff45b5

## Tool areas

- Arrivals: real-time arrivals for DC Metro and NYC Subway stations and DC Metrobus stops (`get_station_predictions`, `get_bus_predictions`).
- Incidents: service disruptions and DC Metro elevator and escalator outages (`get_incidents`, `get_elevator_incidents`).
- Stations: station search, listing by line, full station lists, and transfers (`search_stations`, `get_stations_by_line`, `get_all_stations`, `get_station_transfers`).
- Routes: NYC Subway route detail, DC Metrobus routes and stops (`get_route_info`, `get_bus_routes`, `get_bus_stops`).
- Live positions: DC Metro train positions and Metrobus vehicles (`get_train_positions`, `get_bus_positions`).
- Global capabilities: `find_transit`, `plan_trip`, `get_departures`, `get_service_status`, `get_vehicle_status`. These five tools are registered alongside the 13 compatible tools. DC and NYC are available; SF Bay is dark and reports unavailable.
- For "when is the next train at X", call `get_departures` with `stop` (a station name) and `coverage` in one step. A station complex such as Times Sq-42 St resolves as one place and covers every line in it; different stations that share a name return `ENTITY_AMBIGUOUS` with one candidate per place, so ask the user or pick by context. Rows carry `routeName` and `stopName`.
- NYC departures can include observed trains: `scheduleMatch` is `unscheduled_call` (a reroute) or `unmatched_trip` (not in the timetable). These have a predicted time and no scheduled time. Report them as running, not as scheduled service.
- For "where is my train" or "what trains are at X", call `get_vehicle_status` with a line `ref`, a dated `tripInstanceRef` (from `get_departures` or a `plan_trip` leg), or a station (`stop` name with `coverage`). Each train has `stopStatus` (`stopped_at`, `incoming_at`, `in_transit_to`), `stopName`, `previousStopName` and `headsign`. DC trains have GPS `coordinates`; NYC trains have coordinates only when stopped at a station (`coordinatesSource: stop`), otherwise null. Describe NYC positions by station, never invent a point between stations.
- Use `find_transit` to inspect coverage availability and its planning capability; call `plan_trip` only when both allow planning. When global coverage is unavailable, use `search_stations`, `get_station_predictions` and `get_incidents` for DC/NYC departure or service questions. These legacy tools do not provide a full journey planner. Never assemble a route from departure boards. Preserve `realtime`, `scheduled_only`, or `unavailable` status and source timestamps. Global tools have no Transit Board renderer.
- DC-only: bus tools, `get_train_positions` and `get_elevator_incidents`. NYC-only: `get_route_info` and `get_station_transfers`. A null `minutesAway` means unknown, not zero; retain the returned arrival status.
- Discovery preserves material exact alternatives up to 50 candidates per query or endpoint (100 across a two-endpoint selection). Larger ambiguous sets return `SCOPE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` with no partial choices; narrow the query or supply an exact reference. Non-material fuzzy results honor `limit`.

Public results come from official WMATA (DC Metro and Metrobus) and MTA (NYC Subway) feeds. The dark SF Bay development pipeline uses 511 SF Bay feeds and retains attribution to 511 SF Bay and participating operators.

## Quick connect

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "transit-mcp": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://transitmcp.com/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

## Docs

- [Transit MCP docs](https://transitmcp.com/docs/): client setup, HTTP endpoints, MCP tools, resources and prompts, and data sources.
- [Source code on GitHub](https://github.com/Aarekaz/metro-mcp): MIT licensed.

## Policies

- [Privacy](https://transitmcp.com/privacy/): how anonymous requests, operational telemetry, and provider logs are handled.
- [Terms of Use](https://transitmcp.com/terms/): fair use, rate limits, and live data limits.
- [Support](https://transitmcp.com/support/): documentation, issue reporting, maintainer contact, and security reports.
